title: A cut clip says how many pieces it is in, and a piece can be retimed from the panel
goal: After you cut a recording into pieces, the layers list still shows it as one plain row with no sign it was ever cut, and the only way to change how fast a piece plays is a menu. Put the piece count on the row where you would look for it, and put the speed next to the other properties of the thing you have picked.
notes: Both halves are gaps the 2026-09-20 cutting build left, recorded in queue/audits/2026-09-20-video-cutting.json. (1) UX-PATTERNS D18 and docs/design/video-surface.md 10.5 both say the layers list shows the layer once WITH its piece count; the row is LayersRow.swift and the count is layer.clipPieces?.count, nil-safe and already computed. (2) docs/design/mocks/pages/video-speed.html: "Retiming is a property of the selected clip, so nothing new appears in the chrome" - so it belongs in the Properties panel, not only in the Video menu. EditorState.clipSpeedInHand / setClipSpeedInHand / clipSpeeds are written and wired already (EditorState+ClipBar.swift); this is the panel row over them. ClipPiece.isHeld is the held case.
acceptance: A clip cut into more than one piece shows its piece count on its row in the layers list, and a clip that has never been cut shows nothing extra
Picking a piece on the timeline shows that piece's speed in the Properties panel, next to the other properties of the clip
Changing the speed from the panel and changing it from Video > Speed produce the same result and the same single undo step
A held frame says it is a held frame in the panel rather than showing a speed it does not have

log.note: Half of this landed on 2026-09-21 under speed-a-stretch-up-slow-a-moment-down: there is now a Speed section in the Properties panel (Sources/Photonz/SpeedInspector.swift) showing the piece in hand, its speed, what the retime did and what the sound is doing, with a held frame saying it is a held frame rather than showing a speed. Panel and Video > Speed are the same call (setClipSpeedInHand) so they are the same single undo step. What is LEFT of this task is the first half only: the piece count on the clip's row in the layers list (LayersRow.swift, layer.clipPieces?.count).

Adversarial pass before building. D18 item 3 and video-surface 10.5 say a cut clip is ONE row however many cuts; the audit's rough item asks the row to say how many pieces. Two homes were possible: a badge beside the name, or the caption line under it that componentNote and separationNote already use. Caption line wins: the count is a fact about the layer, not a control, the slot is measured at about 95pt so a badge beside a name would eat the name, and the row already stacks that line without growing (the list measures row height itself). Wording is '3 pieces', not 'Cut into 3 pieces': SeparationLeftover measured the same slot at about eighteen characters and the trim bar already says 'pieces'. The longer sentence goes in the hover. A single piece that has only been retimed says nothing: it was never cut, and the Speed section already says its speed.

Built and verified. (1) ClipPiecesNote (Sources/PhotonzCore/ClipPiecesNote.swift) is the rule: nil under two pieces, '3 pieces' above, longer sentence in the hover. It rides on LayerRowDisplay.piecesNote, read off layer.cuts rather than clipPieces so a row that is not a clip costs one nil check, and LayersRow draws it in the caption line under the name beside componentNote and separationNote. (2) The row's rowDetail carries it too, so a walk can claim it in words. (3) LayerSearch was dropping isSound when it rebuilt a result row, so a piece of sound found by name lost its waveform mark; fixed in the same line that now carries piecesNote, with a test. Verified: 9 new core tests, Scripts/test.sh green at 8919 tests, and the-layers-row-says-how-many-pieces-walk passes with 4 real window captures on an unlocked screen. Ran the neighbours too: 9 cut walks and 11 layers walks all pass, including layers-row-count-perf-walk and layers-lazy-rows-walk. Acceptance 2, 3 and 4 were already done on 2026-09-21 and are re-verified rather than assumed: speed-a-stretch-walk passes, and the panel (SpeedInspector.swift:275) and Video > Speed (EditorCommands.swift:431) are literally the same call, setClipSpeedInHand, so one History step.

Two walks failed in the neighbours I ran and NEITHER is mine: delete-key-drops-a-piece-walk (step 23, delete taken by the window instead of Video > Delete This Piece) and turned-piece-walk (expectBox 3.5pt out). Both were already failing in the 2026-09-21 full sweep and the 2026-09-22 partial, both before this change, and both are already carried by walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-4, so nothing new is filed.

Left rough, not filed: the row says how many pieces and nothing about them, so a clip with a held frame in it reads like three ordinary cuts (the bar badges that on the piece it is true of, which is why it was left); the count is a readout and there is no way from it to the pieces; and this line is drawn in shared code rather than under Releases/Next, which is safe because only Next can cut a clip at all, so a Current document never has cuts to count. All three are in the audit's rough list where the user can react to them.

A cut clip's row in the layers list now says how many pieces it is in (ClipPiecesNote in PhotonzCore, drawn by LayersRow in the caption line under the name), and an uncut one still says nothing extra. The Speed half landed on 2026-09-21 and was re-verified here: speed-a-stretch-walk passes and the panel and Video > Speed are the same call, so one undo step. Verified by 9 new core tests, Scripts/test.sh green at 8919 tests, the new the-layers-row-says-how-many-pieces-walk with four real window captures, and 20 neighbouring cut and layers walks. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-22-video-cutting-piece-count.json. Commit 5ac6ce15, pushed.
